bare_s1.explanation: The unit mainly responds to side views of road vehicles, peaking on the window and door region of cars, police cars, taxis, buses and a fire truck. It responds more weakly to other side-profile bodies held up on legs or wheels, such as gazelles, shorebirds, horses, a dog and a cyclist.

parsed.explanation: The unit mainly responds to side views of road vehicles, peaking on the window and door region of cars, police cars, taxis, buses and a fire truck. parsed.evidence: Vehicles make up 5 of the top 6 images (activation 9-10) and 11 of the top 20, with the box usually on the windows or doors. parsed.missing_data: Activations on frontal or top-down views of cars, on car interiors alone, and on more side-profile animals versus non-profile animals would show whether the core is vehicles or side-profile body shape in general.

parsed.explanation: The unit mainly responds to road vehicles seen from the side, typically at the door and window region of cars, vans, police cars, buses and fire trucks. It responds more weakly to the side-profile bodies of animals such as impala, shorebirds, horses and dogs.
parsed.evidence: Vehicles fill most top slots, including the highest-scoring photos (taxi and sedan at 10, police vans and station wagon at 9), while side-on animals score 7-9 and a random side-view rabbit scores 5. Two shiny curved objects, the trophy (8) and the glass flask (7), don't fit cleanly and may reflect a weaker glossy-curved-surface component.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on vehicles seen head-on or from above, and on non-vehicle side-profile objects, would show whether the unit encodes vehicles specifically or a more general side-view body shape.

F1_s1.explanation: The unit responds most to large, horizontally elongated bodies seen side-on, with smooth curved outlines and glossy, panel-like surfaces broken by darker rectangular openings. It responds more weakly to other side-profile rounded bodies raised on thin supports, and to curved, shiny, reflective forms.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds most to large, horizontally elongated bodies seen side-on, with smooth curved outlines and glossy, panel-like surfaces broken by darker rectangular openings. It responds more weakly to other side-profile rounded bodies raised on thin supports, and to curved, shiny, reflective forms.
parsed.evidence: Photos #1-6, #9-10, #14, #16 and #18 all show long, smooth, shiny bodies in side profile, and the box sits on the upper body and openings. The weaker hits (#7-8, #12-13, #15, #17 at 8-9, and #11, #20 at 7-8) share the side-on rounded body on slender supports or the curved reflective surface, while the random photos stay at 1-5.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on synthetic images that vary glossiness, elongation and side-on viewpoint separately, plus more mid-range (4-6) examples to show where the related extensions end.
